bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for

# igrep

igrep is an interactive search tool that runs a fast search engine in the background and allows you to pick results interactively and open the selected match in your text editor.

Supported platforms: macOS, Linux (Windows reportedly supported).

Usage
-----
ig [OPTIONS] <PATTERN|--type-list> [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  <PATTERN>    Regular expression used for searching.
  <PATHS>...   Files or directories to search. Directories are searched recursively.
               If not specified, searching starts from current directory.

Options (high level):
  --hidden                    Search hidden files and directories.
  --editor <EDITOR>           Text editor used to open selected match.
  --context-viewer <VIEWER>   Context viewer position at startup [default: none]
  --custom-command <COMMAND>  Custom command used to open selected match. Must contain {file_name} and {line_number} tokens.
  -g, --glob <GLOB>           Include files/directories matching the given glob.
  -h, --help                  Print help information
  -i, --ignore-case           Searches case insensitively.
  -L, --follow                Follow symbolic links while traversing directories
  -S, --smart-case            Smart case sensitivity behavior
  -t, --type <TYPE>           Only search files matching TYPE
  -T, --type-not <TYPE>       Do not search files matching TYPE
  --theme <THEME>             UI color theme [default: dark]
  --type-list                 Show all supported file types and their corresponding globs.
  -V, --version               Print version information.
  -w, --word-regexp           Only show matches surrounded by word boundaries
  -F, --fixed-strings         Exact matches with no regex

Keybindings
-----------
q, Esc, Ctrl+c      Quit
? / F1              Open/close the keymap popup
Down / j            Select next match
Up / k              Select previous match
Right / l           Select match in next file
Left / h            Select match in previous file
gg / Home           Jump to the first match
Shift-g / End       Jump to the last match
Enter               Open current file
dd / Delete         Filter out selected match
dw                  Filter out all matches in current file
v                   Toggle vertical context viewer
s                   Toggle horizontal context viewer
+ / -               Increase/decrease context viewer size
F5 / /              Open search pattern popup
n / m / c / a       Sorting and navigation shortcuts

Specifying text editor
----------------------
Order of precedence when selecting editor:
  1. --editor option
  2. $IGREP_EDITOR environment variable
  3. $VISUAL environment variable
  4. $EDITOR environment variable

Custom command example:
  --custom-command "vim +{line_number} {file_name}"
  or set via environment: IGREP_CUSTOM_EDITOR="vim +{line_number} {file_name}"

Installation
------------
Prebuilt binaries are available from the project releases.
Package managers:
  - Homebrew: `brew install igrep`
  - Scoop: `scoop install igrep`
  - Pacman (Arch): `pacman -S igrep`
  - Alpine: `apk add igrep`

License
-------
See the LICENSE file in this repository for license information.

import subprocess, time, sys, os, shlex

def tmux(*args):
    return subprocess.run(["tmux"]+list(args), capture_output=True, text=True)

def start(name="test", cmd=None, width=120, height=40):
    tmux("kill-session","-t",name)
    time.sleep(0.2)
    # new-session
    r=tmux("new-session","-d","-s",name,"-x",str(width),"-y",str(height))
    #print(r)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    if cmd:
        tmux("send-keys","-t",name,cmd,"Enter")
        time.sleep(0.8)

def capture(name="test", esc=False):
    args=["capture-pane","-t",name,"-p"]
    if esc:
        args.insert(1,"-e")
    r=tmux(*args)
    return r.stdout

def send(name, *keys, literal=False):
    for k in keys:
        if literal:
            tmux("send-keys","-t",name,"-l",k)
        else:
            tmux("send-keys","-t",name,k)
        time.sleep(0.35)

def kill(name="test"):
    tmux("kill-session","-t",name)

if __name__=="__main__":
    cmd = "cd /tmp/test1 && TERM=xterm-256color EDITOR=vim /workspace/executable hello"
    start(cmd=cmd, width=100, height=30)
    print(repr(capture()))
    print(capture())
    print("--- ESC ---")
    print(repr(capture(esc=True)[:4000]))
    send("test","q",literal=True)
    time.sleep(0.5)
    print(capture())
    kill()

}

                .value_parser([

                .env("IGREP_CUSTOM_EDITOR"),

        .arg(

                .long("theme")
                .value_name("THEME")
                .help("UI color theme")
                .value_parser(["light", "dark"])
                .default_value("dark"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("ignore_case")
                .short('i')
                .long("ignore-case")
                .help("Searches case insensitively")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("smart_case")
                .short('S')
                .long("smart-case")
                .help("Searches case insensitively if the pattern is all lowercase. Search case sensitively otherwise")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("hidden")
                .short('.')
                .long("hidden")
                .help("Search hidden files and directories. By default, hidden files and directories are skipped")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )

                .short('L')

                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),

                .help("Only show matches surrounded by word boundaries")

                .short('F')
                .long("fixed-strings")
                .help("Exact matches with no regex. Useful when searching for a string full of delimiters")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("multiline")
                .short('U')
                .long("multiline")
                .help("Search with pattern contains newline character ('\\n')")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),

            Arg::new("glob")
                .short('g')
                .long("glob")
                .value_name("GLOB")
                .help("Include files and directories for searching that match the given glob. Multiple globs may be provided")
                .action(ArgAction::Append),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("type_list")
                .long("type-list")
                .help("Show all supported file types and their corresponding globs")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("type_matching")
                .short('t')
                .long("type")
                .value_name("TYPE_MATCHING")
                .help("Only search files matching TYPE. Multiple types may be provided")
                .action(ArgAction::Append),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("type_not")
                .short('T')
                .long("type-not")
                .value_name("TYPE_NOT")
                .help("Do not search files matching TYPE-NOT. Multiple types-not may be provided")
                .action(ArgAction::Append),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("context_viewer")
                .long("context-viewer")
                .value_name("CONTEXT_VIEWER")
                .help("Context viewer position at startup")
                .value_parser(["none", "vertical", "horizontal"])
                .default_value("none"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("sort_by")
                .long("sort")
                .value_name("SORT_BY")
                .help("Sort results, see ripgrep for details")
                .value_parser(["path", "modified", "created", "accessed"]),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("sort_by_reverse")
                .long("sortr")
                .value_name("SORT_BY_REVERSE")
                .help("Sort results reverse, see ripgrep for details")
                .value_parser(["path", "modified", "created", "accessed"]),
        )
}

pub fn parse() -> Args {

    let paths: Vec<PathBuf> = matches
        .get_many::<PathBuf>("paths")
        .map(|values| values.cloned().collect())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let paths_string: Vec<String> = paths
        .iter()
        .map(|path| path.to_str().expect("Not valid UTF-8").to_string())
        .collect();
    Args {
        pattern: matches.get_one::<String>("pattern").cloned(),
        paths_string,
        paths,
        editor: matches.get_one::<String>("editor").cloned(),
        custom_command: matches.get_one::<String>("custom_command").cloned(),
        theme: match matches.get_one::<String>("theme").map(|s| s.as_str()) {
            Some("light") => Theme::Light,
            _ => Theme::Dark,
        },
        ignore_case: matches.get_flag("ignore_case"),
        smart_case: matches.get_flag("smart_case"),
        hidden: matches.get_flag("hidden"),
        follow: matches.get_flag("follow"),
        word_regexp: matches.get_flag("word_regexp"),
        fixed_strings: matches.get_flag("fixed_strings"),
        multiline: matches.get_flag("multiline"),
        globs: matches
            .get_many::<String>("glob")
            .map(|values| values.cloned().collect())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        type_list: matches.get_flag("type_list"),
        type_matching: matches
            .get_many::<String>("type_matching")
            .map(|values| values.cloned().collect())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        type_not: matches
            .get_many::<String>("type_not")
            .map(|values| values.cloned().collect())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        context_viewer: match matches
            .get_one::<String>("context_viewer")
            .map(|s| s.as_str())
        {
            Some("vertical") => ContextViewer::Vertical,
            Some("horizontal") => ContextViewer::Horizontal,
            _ => ContextViewer::None,
        },
        sort_by: matches.get_one::<String>("sort_by").map(|s| sort_by_value(s)),
        sort_by_reverse: matches
            .get_one::<String>("sort_by_reverse")
            .map(|s| sort_by_value(s)),
    }
}

/// A trait for visiting an abstract syntax tree (AST) in depth first order.
///
/// The principle aim of this trait is to enable callers to perform case
/// analysis on an abstract syntax tree without necessarily using recursion.
/// In particular, this permits callers to do case analysis with constant stack
/// usage, which can be important since the size of an abstract syntax tree
/// may be proportional to end user input.
///
/// Typical usage of this trait involves providing an implementation and then
/// running it using the [`visit`] function.
///
/// Note that the abstract syntax tree for a regular expression is quite
/// complex. Unless you specifically need it, you might be able to use the much
/// simpler [high-level intermediate representation](crate::hir::Hir) and its
/// [corresponding `Visitor` trait](crate::hir::Visitor) instead.
pub trait Visitor {
    /// The result of visiting an AST.
    type Output;
    /// An error that visiting an AST might return.
    type Err;

    /// All implementors of `Visitor` must provide a `finish` method, which
    /// yields the result of visiting the AST or an error.
    fn finish(self) -> Result<Self::Output, Self::Err>;

    /// This method is called before beginning traversal of the AST.
    fn start(&mut self) {}

    /// This method is called on an `Ast` before descending into child `Ast`
    /// nodes.
    fn visit_pre(&mut self, _ast: &Ast) -> Result<(), Self::Err> {
        Ok(())
    }

    /// This method is called on an `Ast` after descending all of its child
    /// `Ast` nodes.
    fn visit_post(&mut self, _ast: &Ast) -> Result<(), Self::Err> {
        Ok(())
    }

    /// This method is called between child nodes of an
    /// [`Alternation`](ast::Alternation).
    fn visit_alternation_in(&mut self) -> Result<(), Self::Err> {
        Ok(())
    }

    /// This method is called between child nodes of a concatenation.
    fn visit_concat_in(&mut self) -> Result<(), Self::Err> {
        Ok(())
    }

    /// This method is called on every [`ClassSetItem`](ast::ClassSetItem)
    /// before descending into child nodes.
    fn visit_class_set_item_pre(
        &mut self,
        _ast: &ast::ClassSetItem,
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Err> {
        Ok(())
    }

    /// This method is called on every [`ClassSetItem`](ast::ClassSetItem)

    fn visit_class_set_item_post(
        &mut self,

import sys,subprocess,time; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from helper import *

def run(binpath,args,seq,width=80,height=24,env="TERM=xterm-256color EDITOR=vim",cwd="/tmp/test1"):
    start(f"cd {cwd} && {env} {binpath} {args}",width=width,height=height)
    snaps=[]
    snaps.append((cap(),cap(esc=True)))
    for key,lit in seq:
        send(key,lit=lit)
        snaps.append((cap(),cap(esc=True)))
    kill()
    return snaps
def compare(label,args,seq,**kw):
    a=run(REF,args,seq,**kw); b=run(OUR,args,seq,**kw)
    ok=True
    for i,(x,y) in enumerate(zip(a,b)):
        if x!=y:
            ok=False
            print(f"\nDIFF {label} step {i}")
            print("REF plain:\n",x[0])
            print("OUR plain:\n",y[0])
            if x[0]==y[0]:
                print("plain same, esc differs")
                for lx,ly in zip(x[1].splitlines(),y[1].splitlines()):

    print(label,"OK" if ok else "FAIL")

fn line_infos(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<LineInfo> {
    let mut lines = Vec::new();

                let next_start = content_end + 1;
                lines.push(LineInfo { start, content_end, next_start });
                start = next_start;
            }
            None => {
                lines.push(LineInfo { start, content_end: data.len(), next_start: data.len() });
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    lines
}

fn line_index_for(lines: &[LineInfo], data_len: usize, position: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    if position >= data_len {
        if data_len == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        // A position at the very end belongs to the last, unterminated line.
        // If the data ends in a newline it is a virtual following line.
        if lines
            .last()
            .map(|line| line.next_start > line.content_end)
            .unwrap_or(false)
        {
            return None;
        }
        return lines.len().checked_sub(1);
    }
    lines.iter().position(|line| position >= line.start && position < line.next_start)
}

fn binary_chunk_contains_nul(data: &[u8], position: usize) -> bool {
    // Split the data into line-aligned chunks of at most BUFFER_SIZE bytes,
    // mirroring the line-mode reader, and see whether the chunk containing
    // `position` contains a NUL byte.
    let mut start = 0usize;
    while start < data.len() {
        let mut end = usize::min(data.len(), start + BUFFER_SIZE);
        if end < data.len() {
            match data[start..end].iter().rposition(|byte| *byte == b'\n') {
                Some(pos) => end = start + pos + 1,
                None => {
                    // long line: extend to its end
                    match data[end..].iter().position(|byte| *byte == b'\n') {
                        Some(pos) => end = end + pos + 1,
                        None => end = data.len(),
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if position >= start && position < end {
            return data[start..end].contains(&0);
        }
        if end == start {
            break;
        }
        start = end;
    }
    false
}

fn rgb(r: u8, g: u8, b: u8) -> Color {

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Palette {
    pub foreground: Color,

pub fn palette(theme: &Theme) -> Palette {
    match theme {
        Theme::Dark => Palette {
            foreground: rgb(192, 197, 206),
            comment: rgb(101, 115, 126),
            red: rgb(191, 97, 106),
            orange: rgb(208, 135, 112),

}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Lang {
    Plain,
    Hash,
    Slash,
    Rust,
    Python,
    Html,
}

pub struct Highlighter {
    palette: Palette,
    lang: Lang,
    in_block_comment: bool,
    in_triple: Option<&'static str>,
}

impl Highlighter {
    pub fn new(file_name: &str, first_line: &str, theme: &Theme) -> Self {
        Self {
            palette: palette(theme),
            lang: detect_lang(file_name, first_line),
            in_block_comment: false,
            in_triple: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn highlight_line(&mut self, line: &str) -> Line<'static> {
        if self.lang == Lang::Plain {
            return Line::from(Span::styled(
                line.to_string(),
                Style::default().fg(self.palette.foreground),
            ));
        }
        let spans = self.tokenize(line);
        if spans.is_empty() {
            Line::from(Span::styled(
                String::new(),
                Style::default().fg(self.palette.foreground),
            ))
        } else {
            Line::from(spans)
        }
    }


    fn push_string_content(&self, spans: &mut Vec<Span<'static>>, content: &str) {
        let mut start = 0usize;
        let mut idx = 0usize;
        let bytes = content.as_bytes();
        while idx < bytes.len() {
            if bytes[idx] == b'\\' && idx + 1 < bytes.len() {
                if start < idx {
                    spans.push(Span::styled(
                        content[start..idx].to_string(),
                        Style::default().fg(self.palette.green),
                    ));
                }
                let mut end = idx + 2;
                // \xNN, \uNNNN and \u{...} forms
                if end < bytes.len() && (bytes[end - 1] == b'x' || bytes[end - 1] == b'u') {
                    if end < bytes.len() && bytes[end] == b'{' {
                        while end < bytes.len() && bytes[end] != b'}' {
                            end += 1;
                        }
                        if end < bytes.len() {
                            end += 1;
                        }
                    } else {
                        let max_digits = if bytes[end - 1] == b'x' { 2 } else { 4 };
                        let mut count = 0;
                        while end < bytes.len()
                            && count < max_digits
                            && (bytes[end] as char).is_ascii_hexdigit()
                        {
                            end += 1;
                            count += 1;
                        }
                    }
                }
                spans.push(Span::styled(
                    content[idx..end].to_string(),
                    Style::default().fg(self.palette.cyan),
                ));
                idx = end;
                start = end;
                continue;
            }
            if self.lang == Lang::Python && bytes[idx] == b'{' {
                if let Some(close) = content[idx..].find('}') {
                    if start < idx {
                        spans.push(Span::styled(
                            content[start..idx].to_string(),
                            Style::default().fg(self.palette.green),
                        ));
                    }
                    let end = idx + close + 1;
                    spans.push(Span::styled(
                        content[idx..end].to_string(),
                        Style::default().fg(self.palette.orange),
                    ));
                    idx = end;
                    start = end;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            idx += content[idx..].chars().next().map(|c| c.len_utf8()).unwrap_or(1);
        }
        if start < content.len() {
            spans.push(Span::styled(
                content[start..].to_string(),
                Style::default().fg(self.palette.green),
            ));
        }
    }

fn clean_line(raw_line: &str) -> String {
    let mut text = raw_line;
    if text.ends_with('\n') {
        text = &text[..text.len() - 1];
        if text.ends_with('\r') {
            text = &text[..text.len() - 1];
        }
    }
    text.replace('\t', "    ")
        .chars()
        .filter(|chr| !chr.is_control() && *chr != '\u{200b}' && *chr != '\u{feff}')
        .collect()
}

fn context_block() -> Block<'static> {
    Block::default()
        .borders(Borders::ALL)
        .border_type(BorderType::Rounded)
}

fn visible_range(selected_index: usize, area_height: u16) -> (usize, usize) {
    let half = (area_height as usize) / 2;
    let start = selected_index.saturating_sub(half);
    let relative = selected_index - start;
    (start, relative)
}

fn line_display_width(line: &Line<'_>) -> usize {
    line.spans
        .iter()
        .map(|span| unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr::width(span.content.as_ref()))
        .sum()
}

fn fill_selected_background(
    current_line: &mut Line<'static>,
    selected_background: Color,
    inner_width: usize,
) {
    current_line.style = Style::default().bg(selected_background);
    for span in &mut current_line.spans {
        span.style = span.style.bg(selected_background);
    }
    let text_width = line_display_width(current_line);
    if text_width < inner_width {
        current_line.spans.push(Span::styled(
            " ".repeat(inner_width - text_width),
            Style::default().bg(selected_background),
        ));
    }
}

impl ContextViewer {
    pub fn draw(
        &mut self,
        frame: &mut Frame,
        area: Rect,
        file_name: Option<&str>,
        line_number: Option<u64>,
        selected_background: Color,
        theme: &Theme,
    ) {
        let block = context_block();

        let Some(file_name) = file_name else {
            frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new("").block(block), area);
            return;
        };
        let Some(line_number) = line_number else {
            frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new("").block(block), area);
            return;
        };

        let lines = self.lines_for(file_name, theme).to_vec();

        let selected_index = (line_number as usize).saturating_sub(1);
        let (start, relative) = visible_range(selected_index, area.height);
        let mut visible: Vec<Line<'static>> = lines
            .into_iter()
            .skip(start)
            .take(area.height as usize)
            .collect();

        {
            let current_line = &mut visible[relative];
            let inner_width = area.width.saturating_sub(2) as usize;
            fill_selected_background(current_line, selected_background, inner_width);
        }

        let widget = Paragraph::new(visible).block(block);
        frame.render_widget(widget, area);
    }

fn detect_lang(file_name: &str, first_line: &str) -> Lang {
    let base = file_name.rsplit('/').next().unwrap_or(file_name);
    if base == "Makefile" || base == "makefile" || base == "GNUmakefile" {
        return Lang::Hash;
    }
    if first_line.starts_with("#!") {
        if first_line.contains("python") {
            return Lang::Python;
        }
        if first_line.contains("sh") || first_line.contains("bash") || first_line.contains("zsh") {
            return Lang::Shell;
        }
    }
    let ext = base.rsplit('.').next().unwrap_or("");
    if base == ext {
        return Lang::Plain;
    }
    match ext {
        "rs" => Lang::Rust,
        "py" | "pyi" => Lang::Python,
        "c" | "h" | "cpp" | "cc" | "cxx" | "hpp" | "hh" | "hxx" => Lang::C,
        "js" | "jsx" | "ts" | "tsx" | "mjs" | "cjs" => Lang::Js,
        "go" => Lang::Go,
        "json" => Lang::Json,
        "java" | "cs" | "kt" | "kts" | "scala" | "swift" | "php" => Lang::Slash,
        "sh" | "bash" | "zsh" => Lang::Shell,
        "md" | "markdown" | "mdown" | "mdx" => Lang::Markdown,
        "rb" | "pl" | "pm" | "yml" | "yaml" | "toml" | "ini" | "cfg" | "conf" => Lang::Hash,
        "html" | "htm" | "xml" | "xhtml" | "svg" => Lang::Html,
        "txt" | "text" | "" => Lang::Plain,
        _ => Lang::Plain,
    }
}

//! A small stateful wrapper around a Ratatui [`List`] that keeps the
//! selected match visible without relying solely on the renderer's
//! built in offset handling.
//!
//! The results in this application are a flat list in which file names
//! and the matches inside those files are separate rows.  When the
//! selection moves upwards out of the viewport, showing the item
//! immediately above the selected match is useful because that item
//! is often the name of the file to which the match belongs.  The
//! custom offset calculation in this module therefore leaves one row
//! above a selection that has scrolled off the top of the viewport,
//! while a selection that scrolls off the bottom is placed on the
//! last visible row.
//!
//! The list itself is stateless with respect to the search results:
//! callers rebuild the items for every frame and pass the currently
//! selected row (if any) to [`ScrollOffsetList::draw`].  This type
//! only remembers the Ratatui list state and the scroll offset that
//! was used for the previous frame.

use ratatui::{
    prelude::*,
    widgets::{List, ListItem, ListState},
};

//! A small stateful wrapper around a Ratatui [`List`] that keeps the
//! selected match visible without relying solely on the renderer's
//! built in offset handling.
//!
//! The results in this application are a flat list in which file names
//! and the matches inside those files are separate rows.  When the
//! selection moves upwards out of the viewport, showing the item
//! immediately above the selected match is useful because that item
//! is often the name of the file to which the match belongs.  The
//! custom offset calculation in this module therefore leaves one row
//! above a selection that has scrolled off the top of the viewport,
//! while a selection that scrolls off the bottom is placed on the
//! last visible row.
//!
//! The list itself is stateless with respect to the search results:
//! callers rebuild the items for every frame and pass the currently
//! selected row (if any) to [`ScrollOffsetList::draw`].  This type
//! only remembers the Ratatui list state and the scroll offset that
//! was used for the previous frame.
//!
//! Offset transitions
//! ------------------
//!
//! The offset is deliberately updated only when the selected row
//! would otherwise leave the viewport.  Moving the selection
//! inside the rows that are already visible therefore does not
//! scroll the list at all, which avoids the viewport jumping on
//! every key press.
//!
//! When the selection moves below the final visible row, the new
//! offset is the smallest offset that puts the selection back
//! inside the viewport.  In terms of the selected index (`s`),
//! the previous offset (`o`) and the number of visible rows
//! (`h`), that is `s + 1 - h`.
//!
//! When the selection moves above the first visible row, the
//! new offset is one less than the selected index (or zero for
//! the first item).  As described above, retaining that extra
//! row is particularly useful in this application because the
//! row above a match is often its file name, but the rule is
//! applied uniformly rather than by inspecting the kind of row.
//!
//! Resizing the terminal does not reset the offset.  The same
//! visibility calculation is run with the new viewport height on
//! the next frame, so a taller viewport simply reveals more
//! rows after the existing first visible row, while a shorter
//! viewport scrolls only if the selected row would otherwise
//! be hidden.
//!
//! Callers are responsible for resetting this state when they
//! replace the entire list, for example after starting a new
//! search.  Filtering items out of an existing list deliberately
//! does not reset it, preserving the user's place in the list.
